content.text: The required check found one failure, isolated to `redact/TestBetterleaksDoesNotPoisonGitEnvironment`: its generated `go.mod` was malformed while invoking `go run`. All subagent-related unit/integration packages passed. I’m treating this as a real gate failure and reproducing it narrowly before deciding whether it is environmental or actionable.

Root cause is confirmed and deterministic: the test writes an unquoted local `replace` path into a temporary `go.mod`; this worktree’s path contains spaces, so Go parses it as multiple tokens. The failure is unrelated to the subagent implementation, but it blocks the repository’s mandatory commit gate. I’ll make the minimal test-harness correction as its own commit concern, then re-run the narrow regression and the full gate.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Go module files permit quoted local replacement paths; quoting is the correct serialization boundary, not path escaping by hand.
- The existing regression test is already the right red test: it fails specifically because the harness cannot represent this repository path. No production behavior needs to change.
- Repository search found no shared helper or duplicate construction pattern, so a one-line `strconv.Quote` at the serialization site is the smallest fix.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

why do you need to commit

Because one of the two features specifically handles a background subagent making a commit mid-task. Entire creates the durable checkpoint that appears in the UI when a commit occurs.

- Trail 1076 can be partly tested without committing by inspecting the parent’s subagent task record.
- Trail 1077 inherently requires a commit to test commit-to-session linkage.
- Seeing the result in the remote UI would eventually require publishing the branch/checkpoint metadata too.

I assumed you wanted the full end-to-end path. No commit was made. I can instead stop at local session/task-record inspection and remove the temporary changes if you prefer.
yes, okay proceed

Understood. I’ll proceed with the controlled commits, inspect each resulting checkpoint locally, and stop before any remote push unless UI publication requires your separate approval.

I’m reusing the commit-quality and verification workflows so each scenario stays isolated and the evidence is easy to interpret.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- A commit is the boundary where Entire condenses live session state into a durable checkpoint.
- Keeping “parent commits child work” and “child commits its own work” in separate commits lets us distinguish the two tracking paths in both metadata and UI.
